ai.example1: Read START_HERE.md and DATASET_INVENTORY.md, and sum up in five lines which file tells what.
ai.example2: Using analysis/activities.csv, make a table of the number of runs and the total distance (km) per month. Do not count rows with an empty distance, and give their number separately. Write the formulas too.
ai.example3: From analysis/activities.csv, compute the average pace (min/km) per month. Write the numbers of rows used and left out, and the formulas. Do not treat empty values as 0.
ai.example4: In activities_monthly.csv, one row is one activity, and dates go to the month. Count the activities and add up the distance (km) per month yourself, and make a table. Write the formulas too.
ai.lede: An AI's answer is not always right. Always check the answer against the output.
ai.step1: It is the entry of the output. Read START_HERE.md, then DATASET_INVENTORY.md, then ANALYSIS_HANDOFF.md.
ai.step2: The whole output contains IDs, exact dates and times, notes, and so on. Do not give the output folder as it is to an outside AI.
ai.step2_title: First, on this computer or with an AI you trust
ai.step3: Decide the period, the grouping, the denominator, and how to treat empty values, and ask one question at a time.
ai.step3_title: Ask one thing at a time
ai.step4: Create it with the check box in box 3. Dates go to the month, with six fields only. Before you give it, check the receiver and what is in it.
ai.step4_title: For an outside AI, the summary that can be given to an AI
ai.step5: Compare with START_HERE.md whether a missing value was taken as 0, and whether the formulas and counts match. Do not use the answers as medical or training advice.
ai.tag_external: For an outside AI (the summary that can be given to an AI)
ai.tag_local: For this computer or an AI you trust

export.heading: This export
extract.help: Needed only for an extracted folder: if the extraction stopped partway, files are missing from the normalization and the results change.

faq.attach_a: No. Do not attach or paste the export, the output, rows of records, IDs, file names, paths, exact dates and times, locations, or notes. The report of “If something is wrong” opens with safe values only.
faq.attach_q: May I attach my export to a report on GitHub?
faq.date_a: One normalization computes dates and times in one timezone (Asia/Tokyo by default). Records made while travelling are not in the local time of that place. You can change it with “Timezone for local dates and times” in box 3.
faq.date_q: Why is a date one day off from Garmin Connect?
faq.exit_a: 0 is “Normalized” (nothing was left out), 3 is “Normalized with part of the input left out” (files that could not be read, for example, were left out; the output can be used), and 2 is “Could not normalize” (no output is created).
faq.exit_q: What do the exit codes 0, 3, and 2 mean?
faq.place_a: By default, in GarminRunningData in your home folder: each output is a new folder in it, and the Snapshot Store is its folder snapshots. If GarminRunningData is not there, it is made when you normalize. Documents and the Desktop are not used, since iCloud Drive or OneDrive may copy them to the cloud. Back it up with Time Machine or the like.
faq.place_q: Where are the output and the store made?
faq.remember_a: Only the names of the places of the Snapshot Store, of the folder for the output, and of earlier outputs (the latest 10), and whether “Show tips” is on, in a file of settings on this computer. It remembers the places when a normalization makes its output. It does not remember what is in your data, or where the export is. Forget them with “Forget the remembered settings…” in the bar at the bottom.
faq.send_a: No. The export and the output are handled on this computer only. Before you give them to a person or an AI, check what is in them.
faq.send_q: Does this app send my data to an AI or anywhere else?
faq.time_a: Usually not. For a ZIP file, the time of the file is filled in, and for an extracted folder, the time of its newest file. The Snapshots are in the order of these times, so change it only when its order among the other Snapshots is not the real one.
faq.time_q: Should I change the download time?
faq.values_a: The normalization does not stop. In the normalized table, only the fields whose values differ are left empty and marked, and every value is kept in the records (audit). A warning tells you about it.
faq.values_q: What happens when a day has two different values?
faq.window_a: If you close the window, the normalization goes on while the terminal stays open. Open the same address again to see it. When no normalization is running and no window has been connected for 10 minutes, this app quits. The result of a normalization stays in the output folder. While the computer sleeps, the normalization does not progress.
faq.window_q: What if I close the window or the computer sleeps during a normalization?
faq.zip_a: Yes. Choose the downloaded ZIP file with “Choose ZIP file…”; it needs no check of the extraction. ZIP files inside it are read one level deep.
faq.zip_q: Can I use the downloaded ZIP file as it is?
finding.activities_empty: The Activities files hold no Activity that can be used.
finding.activities_unreadable: The Activities files cannot be read, such as a file that is too large or damaged.
finding.files_left_out: Some files cannot be read, such as a damaged ZIP file or a file that is too large. A normalization leaves them out; START_HERE.md gives their number, and run_manifest.json lists them.
finding.files_left_out_count: Files that cannot be read: {count}, such as a damaged ZIP file or a file that is too large. A normalization leaves them out; START_HERE.md gives their number, and run_manifest.json lists them.
finding.input_directory: The input is not an existing folder or ZIP file, or it is a symbolic link.
finding.input_duplicate_sources: The input holds the same Export more than once, such as the ZIP file and the folder extracted from it. A normalization reads it once and gives a warning.
forget.done: The remembered settings are forgotten. The store and the files of the outputs are still there.
forget.question: Forget the remembered settings?
forget.text: This app forgets the Snapshot Store, the folder for the output, the list of earlier outputs, and whether “Show tips” is on. It does not delete the store or the files of the outputs. The next launch goes as a first launch does (a store that is not in the default place must be opened again).
help.ai_heading: Using the normalized data with AI
help.get_note: This app does not sign in to Garmin or request the export for you.
help.get_step1: On the Data Management page of your Garmin account, request an export of all your account data (Account Data Export). The page: {part}
help.get_step2: Garmin takes a while to prepare it. When it is ready, Garmin lets you know; download the ZIP file as the message says, and keep the message until the download has finished.
help.get_step3: The downloaded ZIP file can be used in box 1 as it is, without extracting it.
help.heading: Help
help.report_heading: If something is wrong: report it on GitHub
help.step_export_text: Choose the export downloaded from Garmin with “Choose ZIP file…” or “Choose extracted folder…”. It is checked right away. For an extracted folder, check that the extraction finished, and tick the box.
help.step_output_text: Check where the output is created, its name, and the timezone for local dates and times, and press “Use these settings” (from the second launch, they are set by themselves while they stay as last time).
help.step_results_text: Yellow rows are warnings. Before you use the output, read in START_HERE.md what was left out and what the warnings say.
help.step_run_text: Wait until it finishes. If you cancel before it has finished, no output folder is created.
help.step_snapshot: Set the Snapshots and how to normalize
help.step_snapshot_text: Check how to normalize and the store, and press “Use these settings” (from the second launch, they are set by themselves while they stay as last time). To import into the Snapshots, also check the name of the Snapshot and the download time in box 1.
help.steps_lede: Set the four boxes in the order of their numbers. Press a step to highlight its box.
hint.export: Tip: The ZIP file downloaded from Garmin can be used as it is, without extracting it.
hint.output: Tip: Where the output is created and its name. Usually they can stay as they are.
hint.run: Tip: When everything is ready, press “Run normalization”. When it has finished, open the output folder.
hint.snapshot: Tip: Importing into the Snapshots normalizes this export with the ones imported before. What you import stays and is used from then on; to only try this app, choose “Normalize this export only (no import)”. The store can usually stay as it is.
how.single_note: This way does not use the store: only this export is normalized, and it is not imported into the Snapshots.
how.snapshots: Import into the Snapshots and normalize them together (recommended)
import.label: Name of the Snapshot
import.label_help: Up to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores, or hyphens. By default, the date of the download.
import.time_from_folder: It was filled in from the newest file in the folder, which is near the time when the export was made. The Snapshots are in the order of these times. You can change it.
import.time_from_zip: It was filled in from the time of the ZIP file. The Snapshots are in the order of these times. You can change it.
import.time_help: The Snapshots are in the order of these times.
info.exit_0: Nothing was left out. If there are warnings, check what they say.
info.exit_2: The normalization stopped. No output folder was created. The red box says why and what to do next.
info.exit_3: Something was left out, such as files that could not be read. The output can be used; the warnings and START_HERE.md say what was left out.
info.exit_3_label: 3: Normalized with part of the input left out
info.exit_foot: Besides files that could not be read, 3 also comes when rows that cannot be used, such as rows without a date or a number or rows out of range, were left out.
info.exit_text: The same numbers as when you normalize with the command line. Use them to compare with a result of the command line, or when you ask for help.
info.how_foot: They match snapshot register and snapshot run-all, and run-all, of the command line.
info.how_single: Makes the output from this export only, without the store. Nothing is imported into the Snapshots.
info.how_snapshots: Copies this export into the store, then normalizes it together with the existing Snapshots. The output includes what was imported before.
info.pack_foot: Off at first. It is the same as --external-safe-pack (the External-safe Pack) of the command line.
info.pack_in: A table with one row per activity (safe/activities_monthly.csv) and six columns: the month, the activity type, the sport type, the distance (m), the duration (seconds), and the number of laps. Dates are reduced to the month (one row per activity, not monthly totals). With the files that describe it, five files in all go into one ZIP file (analysis/external_safe_handoff.zip).
info.pack_note: It is never sent automatically. Before you give it, check the receiver and what is in it.
info.pack_out: Exact dates and times, IDs, paths and names of files, notes, locations, heart rate, power, cadence, training effect and load, Gear, Personal Records, FIT details, and daily data such as sleep and HRV.
info.pack_use: When you want to ask an outside AI about how much and how often you ran each month.
info.place_backup: Since it is not copied to a cloud, no copy to restore is made by itself. Back it up with Time Machine or the like.
info.place_other: Choose another place with “Choose…”. A folder that a cloud may copy is marked in yellow. The places that a normalization used are used again at the next launch (forget them with “Forget the remembered settings…” in the bar at the bottom).
info.place_text: By default, the outputs and the store go in GarminRunningData in your home folder: each output is a new folder in it, and the store is its folder snapshots.
info.place_why: iCloud Drive or OneDrive may be set to copy them to the cloud by themselves. Then your personal data leaves this computer.
info.place_why_label: Why not Documents or the Desktop
info.store_care1: This app never changes the files of an imported Snapshot, and never deletes them by itself.
info.store_care2: It holds your personal data. Keep it on this computer, in a place that only you can read. By default it is the folder snapshots in GarminRunningData in your home folder. Documents and the Desktop are not used, since iCloud Drive may copy them to the cloud.
info.store_care3: Since it is not copied to a cloud, back it up with Time Machine or the like. Before you back it up, check it with “Check the Snapshots”, and check it again after you restore it.
info.store_foot: The same store as the snapshot commands of the command line use.
info.store_text: A folder that keeps a copy of each export. Every normalization uses all the Snapshots in it together.
info.timezone_care1: One normalization computes in one timezone. Records made while travelling are not in the local time of that place either.
info.timezone_care2: Another timezone can move the day of records that span midnight, such as sleep. To compare with an earlier output, use the same timezone.
info.timezone_foot: The same as --timezone of the command line.
info.timezone_text: Sets in the time of which region the dates and times of the records are given. The default is Asia/Tokyo.
info.tools_bundle: A ZIP file with six summary files to add to a request for help. It contains no rows of your records, paths, file names, identifiers, exact times, or coordinates. Nothing is uploaded: it is saved where you choose, by default next to the output folder.
info.tools_check: Checks that this output folder is as the normalization made it, with nothing missing or changed.
info.tools_foot: They match validate-handoff, doctor --run-output, and support-bundle of the command line.
info.tools_note: The counts in it can still show how much you use your device. Review all six files before you share it.

store.label: Snapshot Store
store.list_note: The Snapshots are in the order of their export times, which were recorded when they were imported; for those imported on this page, the download times. “Files” is the number of files of the export of each Snapshot, which the store keeps; it shows “—” before the import.
store.new: There is no store here yet. It is created here when you normalize.
store.same_note: If the export has the same content as one in the store, the import finds that out and adds no new Snapshot.

summary.output_done: Created {name} in {parent} (the name field holds the name for the next normalization)
summary.snapshot_import: Imports into the Snapshots and normalizes them with the {count} existing ones
summary.snapshot_new: Creates the store, imports the first Snapshot, and normalizes it
summary.snapshot_new_done: Created the store and imported the first Snapshot
summary.snapshot_single: No Snapshots: only this export is normalized

tools.heading: If something is wrong
tools.report_note: You can check the values before anything is sent
tools.summary: Output check, Support Bundle, and report on GitHub
warning.activity_fit_link_ambiguous: {name}: some activities or FIT sessions had more than one equally matching candidate, so no link was decided for them ({count}). audit/activity_fit_linkage.json lists each with the reason ({code}).
warning.daily_metrics_review: {name}: some daily metric values need review ({count}), such as a value without a date ({code}).
warning.data_file_left_out: {name}: some files could not be read and were left out ({count}). run_manifest.json lists them with the reason ({code}).
warning.data_row_left_out: {name}: some rows lacked a required value, such as a date or a usable identifier, or were not records, such as a number in a list of records, and were left out ({count}). START_HERE.md gives their number for each table, and the audit files count them by reason ({code}).
warning.data_text_repaired: {name}: some text held a broken character, such as an emoji cut in half. It is written with the replacement character � in its place, and run_manifest.json lists the files ({code}).
warning.data_value_invalid: {name}: some values had a form that their field does not take, such as text where a number belongs ({count}). Those fields are left empty, and every such value is kept in the audit files ({code}).
warning.fit_parse_incomplete: {name}: some FIT files could not be read completely ({count}). They were left out, and nothing was guessed ({code}).
warning.input_duplicate_sources: {name}: the input held the same export more than once, such as the ZIP and the folder extracted from it. It was read once ({code}).
warning.lactate_candidates: {name}: in some places, the candidates for the lactate threshold could not be narrowed to one ({count}). All are kept in the audit files, and none was chosen ({code}).
warning.optional_family_empty: {name}: this data was in the export but produced no records ({code}).
warning.optional_family_not_present: {name}: this data was not in the export, so its tables are empty. If you do not use this data, there is nothing to do ({code}).
warning.records_not_in_latest_snapshot: {name}: some records are not in the latest export ({count}). They are kept, and the audit files show the last export that had each of them ({code}).
warning.relationship_invalid_link: {name}: some personal records have a link to an activity that is missing, malformed, or disagrees ({count}). They are kept with the link unresolved, and nothing was guessed ({code}).
warning.relationship_unresolved: {name}: some links between datasets point to records that are not in the output ({count}). They are kept with the link unresolved, and nothing was guessed ({code}).
warning.values_disagree: {name}: some records have values that disagree ({count}). Those fields are left empty and marked, and every value is kept in the audit files; none was chosen ({code}).
warning.values_updated: {name}: a later export changed some records or removed some links ({count}), such as the name of an activity. The tables have the latest values, and the earlier values are kept in the audit files ({code}).
words.bundle_text: A ZIP file with six summary files, for when something is wrong. It contains no rows of your records and no paths.
words.code_text: The code in brackets at the end of a warning or of a reason for a stop, such as OPTIONAL_FAMILY_NOT_PRESENT, names the reason. Use it to look the reason up in the guide, or in a report.
words.dataset_text: One table of a fixed form that the normalization makes, such as Activities or Sleep.
words.exit_text: 0 = Normalized, 3 = Normalized with part of the input left out, 2 = Could not normalize. The numbers are the same as when you normalize with the command line.
words.fit_text: A file (.fit) in which the watch records the details of an activity and more.
words.how_text: Whether to import the export into the Snapshots and normalize them together, which is the default, or to normalize this export only. The existing Snapshots can also be normalized again without an export.
words.normalize_text: Turning a Garmin export into tables and files of a fixed form that are easy to analyze.
words.os_text: The basic software that runs your computer, such as macOS, Windows, or Linux. The dialogs to choose a file or a folder are those of the OS.
words.output_check_text: Checking that the output folder is as the normalization made it, with nothing missing or changed.
words.pack: Summary that can be given to an AI
words.pack_text: A ZIP file with a table of six Activity fields, with dates reduced to the month (the External-safe Pack). It is for giving data to an outside AI.
words.relationship_text: How rows of different datasets belong together, such as an activity and its gear, or an activity and its FIT file. The output check checks these links.
words.snapshot_text: A copy of one export. Snapshots are ordered by the times of their exports, and every normalization uses all of them together.
words.start_here_text: The entry file of the output folder. It says how to read the output and explains what was left out and the warnings.
words.store_text: The folder that holds the Snapshots. By default, the folder snapshots in GarminRunningData in your home folder.
words.uds_text: Garmin's daily summaries: steps, distance, calories, heart rate, Body Battery, and stress.
